result.label: greatbole seed
result.description: A single seed from a greatbole fruit. Planted beside open water it grows with startling speed into a young greatbole — and, in centuries no living thing will see out, into an ancient one again. To the Wildsteam Clan, planting one is a sacrament.

result.label: greatbole
result.description: A single grey-brown column so broad at the base that its fluting reads as separate trunks fused together, rising far past every other crown before opening into one horizontal raft of paddle leaves. Bark in long vertical plates that shed. Nothing grows in its shadow, so it stands in a clearing of its own making. Given centuries and left uncut, a greatbole like this one becomes something else entirely — a trunk too vast to still be called a tree.

result.label: greatbole core
result.description: The living heart of a Greatbole — the one cell of it that never goes still, and never mines out. Everything the tree does starts here.

result.label: dhokkur
result.description: Half the outcrops on the skirts are stone. The other half are waiting for rain. A dormant dhokkur sits out the still heat as a hill of banked obsidian plates, ash drifted into its seams, and the survey crews learn the difference the day the sky opens: the hill stands up. It walks its own path -- the same path, worn a thousand bursts deep -- drinking the scald straight off its back while everything else on the mountain runs for a roof. It is not angry. It has never needed to be. Its hide turns the boiling rain, and the boiling rain is the worst thing this mountain knows how to say.

fields.wakeMessage: The rain is falling and a hill on the skirts has stood up: a {0} is walking.

result.label: dhokkur track
result.description: Ground worn to a black glassy polish by something enormous walking the same line, rain after rain. Nothing grows on it. Whatever made it will be back.

result.label: aerosol screen
result.description: A projector that holds a dome of still, clean air over everything inside it. Blocks toxic fallout, toxic weather and settling film. It does nothing against bullets, heat or cold. Burns dielectric gel; without it the dome shrinks to half.

result.label: settled film
result.description: A pale grey film of fine war dust, settled out of a still sky. It keeps every footprint pressed into it until the wind comes back.

result.label: chotrix
result.description: A lean, low, long-limbed scavenger that ate the old line's light-bending lacquer and carries it in its hide. Standing or stalking, it cannot be seen. It shows when it strikes, and for a few seconds after. It goes for lone small animals and lone people in the dark, never a group, and runs after one bite if it is hurt. Its hide still holds lacquer.

fields.label: condenser buyer
fields.description: A wealthy collector who wants the old gorrask alive for its fighting pit. Non-hostile; fallback: the most advanced non-hostile faction.

fields.label: condenser settlers
fields.description: Farmers who live by the old gorrask's water. Non-hostile; fallback: the friendliest non-hostile faction at or below industrial tech.

fields.label: condenser hunters
fields.description: Trophy hunters who want the old gorrask's shell for the boast. Hostile; fallback: a permanent-enemy faction first.

fields.label: oorrik
fields.description: A single oorrik is nothing — a wet-mouthed sliver of a thing barely bigger than the grains it moves through. A mound's worth of them is a different problem: dozens surfacing in the same half-second across ten metres of sand, each one too small to hit and too many to count. Nothing about any one of them is dangerous. That was never the point.

fields.label: kneel ollim
fields.description: The ollim's other body. Where the tall form is a bone-white truncate, the kneel form is the shield: a low, swept, wind-aligned dome that grows where the buried moisture is too thin to fund a tower, which is most places the ollim grows at all. A bone-field usually carries one tower and a scatter of kneels, all one organism's slow children. It casts a hard black crescent of shade a grain animal can live in; a loomma cannot, the shadow is too small.

fields.label: disturbed sand
fields.description: A shallow collapsed funnel ringed with slumped crust. A low furrow runs into it and stops. Something under the sand came up here and took whatever was standing on it.

fields.label: bileworm
fields.description: A vast, slow slug in mottled grey-green skin, ribbed along its pale underside and pitted with a row of dark breathing holes down each flank, its two eye-stalks nodding over a cluster of yellow, finger-like mouthparts. It breathes out a foul, corrosive gas wherever it goes: mostly harmless to the living, but murder on the dead. Anything it passes near rots in minutes into a black, reeking fluid, which the bileworm then happily drinks.

fields.label: juggernaut beetle
fields.description: A heavy, domed beetle in dull slate-black armour, its back one great crown of overlapping plates and its head swept back into a long curved horn. Pale blue light glows in the joints of its limbs and around its jaws, and one oversized hooked forelimb is held ready in front of it. It walks slowly, because nothing it meets has ever made it hurry.

fields.label: electric gryllotalpa
fields.description: A large bioengineered insectoid. Designed to destroy the mechanoid. The discharge organs are highly developed and capable of releasing focused arcs to attack distant enemies. Focused arcs can cause double damage to the mechanoid.

fields.label: electric tick
fields.description: A medium bioengineered insectoid. Designed to destroy the mechanoid. The growth rate is extremely rapid, but as a result, the lifespan is very short. The discharge organ occupies more than half of the body tissue and releases a strong electric current upon death.

fields.label: rimclaw
fields.description: A low, armoured scavenger the colour of old rust, its back a stack of jagged overlapping plates and its eyes two orange beads on short stalks. One enormous saw-toothed claw hangs from its side; it snaps the claw shut on whatever it catches and carries on. It picks across slag and scrap on sharp, dark-tipped legs, and nothing metal or meaty is safe near it.
